md_northwest_branch.blurb: Northwest Branch is a wooded bouldering area along the Northwest Branch of the Anacostia River in Silver Spring, a short drive north of Washington, DC. Almost everything is bouldering, spread across North Bank and South Bank groupings such as the Pipeline Area, Long Wall and Tulip Area. Grades span V0 up to about V10, with the bulk between V0 and V5, so newer climbers and strong ones both find projects. Many of the blocks are true boulders with top-outs, which is unusual near DC. Walk-ins are short, and a crash pad and a spotter are advised. Heavy traffic has polished some holds.

az_mcdowell_mountains.blurb: The McDowell Mountains rise in northeast Scottsdale on the edge of the Phoenix area, inside a large desert preserve. The rock is rough-grained desert granite in piles of domes and formations, resembling Joshua Tree. Traditional climbing leads, with a modest number of sport routes and a few boulders. Grades run from easy up to about 5.12, with most between 5.7 and 5.10. Sven Slab has beginner-friendly lines, while Gardener's Wall and Tom's Thumb are among the best-known formations. Approaches range from a half mile to two miles of hiking. The main season runs from winter through spring, because the rock gets scorching hot in summer.

ar_north_side_3.blurb: North Side is one of four sections of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, a sandstone climbing destination in north-central Arkansas between Jasper and Ponca. Sport climbing is the main event, with a sizable set of boulder problems and a smaller number of trad lines. Roped climbs mostly sit between 5.7 and 5.12, with the heart around 5.7 to 5.10, and boulder problems run from VB to about V10. The North Forty holds the most climbing, with sport routes and a separate boulder group. Most roped lines face south, though there are plenty of exceptions that let you chase shade through the day.

ca_hwy_33_ojai_bouldering.blurb: Hwy 33/Ojai Bouldering gathers boulder fields in and around Ojai on California's Central Coast and up along Highway 33, nearly all of it bouldering. Most of the climbing is on Pine Mountain, where a sandstone boulder field stretches along a ridgeline at roughly 7,000 feet, with sub-areas such as Happy Hunting Grounds, Picnic Area Boulders and Enlightenment Ridge. The Hideout is the next-largest area. Grades run from V0 to V11, mostly V0 to V6, with a big share of easy problems, so it suits a wide range of boulderers.

ma_dyke_s_pond_gloucester.blurb: Dyke's Pond is a wooded boulder field on Cape Ann in Gloucester, on Massachusetts' North Shore, set in Mt. Anne Park. It is nearly all bouldering on granite, with big boulders scattered through the trees and a short walk in. The problems are grouped into North, East, West and South Sides, with the North Side the largest. Grades run from V0 up to about V7, and the bulk sit between V3 and V6. Some boulders are overgrown, so a brush helps, and local grades across Cape Ann can feel hard for the number.

bc_hunter_creek_bouldering.blurb: Hunter Creek is a bouldering area in British Columbia's Fraser Valley, made up of large granite boulders scattered through a forest beneath a slide area. It is pure bouldering, split into many named sectors such as The Warm Up Sector, Sleight of Hand, Goldfinger and Bear Skull. Grades run from VB to V11, with most problems between V1 and V6 and a solid tail of harder lines, so it suits newer climbers and strong boulderers alike. The granite is gritty and landings can be uneven and wooded, so several pads are useful. Shade from the trees helps in summer, and climbing is possible in most months apart from heavy rain.
